choices.reason: This β-keto ester measured 19.45/45.11 mL at 10/1 and 44.45/81.20 mL at 20/1 (5b445b457a8b897a2d6c, ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f). A 5/1 result locates the start of the steep rise; V/ul differs among records.

The conjugated ketone measured 13.35/35.72 mL at 20/1 and 28.20/68.68 mL at 50/1 (b7fffd840d208b29776c, c9bef93a79964dc6ede1). Its unexpectedly high 1/1 prediction, 28.51/66.26 mL, tests a possible model condition blind spot.
For that same ketone, the 10/1 prediction is 5.91/18.30 mL. Measuring it alongside the selected 1/1 condition and observed 20/1 result tests the model's nonmonotone lower-ratio curve.
Phenylpyridine measured 15.66/32.11 mL at 10/1 and 26.27/81.78 mL at 50/1 (810b065b0b86ff8c9aae, 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4). The 20/1 measurement tests where its V2 and interval width expand.

The enamine ester measured 29.26/109.68 mL at 20/1 with DCM loading (5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d). This PE-loaded 20/1 case tests transfer across loading conditions, though V/ul and loading volume also change.

The enamine ester's measured V2 climbs from 36.80 to 60.45 to 109.68 mL across 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1 (10f01f359bc6067d009f, a2f83665cfe821271b30, 5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d). A 0/1 result tests its strong-eluent endpoint.
Nitrobenzophenone at 50/1 measured V1 4.49 mL and V2 81.30 mL, an unusually wide interval (b514312eda7950cdcf1c). A 20/1 result, with 10/1 pending, tests how that interval develops.
Para-amino ethyl benzoate measured 26.80/57.07 mL at 5/1, far later than its prior prediction (9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb). The predicted 11.00/20.49 mL at 2/1 tests whether the change is steep.

Phenylpropanol rose sharply between measured 2/1 and 5/1 conditions (53c1be5b96937954b9fa, 45a1b11ae63f2dab2e48). Naphthylmethanol at 5/1 tests transfer to another aromatic alcohol; molecular and loading conditions differ.

A para-amino ester measured much later than predicted at 5/1 (9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb). This aminobenzonitrile at 1/1 pairs with a pending 5/1 result to test whether the polar amino scaffold has a similarly steep response; transfer is uncertain.

Naphthyl acetate measured 5.23/13.28 mL at 2/1 and 30.46/50.78 mL at 50/1 (f17690c586ce5d166eb0, c80022254967f6a925f3). The 20/1 measurement tests the interpolation and earlier high-ratio underprediction.
This trifluoromethoxy phenol at 2/1 pairs with a pending 5/1 result. It tests a same-molecule hydroxyl-containing condition contrast; there is no supplied measurement for this molecule yet.
Ethyl nicotinate measured 41.71/106.06 mL at 10/1, far above the prior prediction (c76d0420b34df595c0c9). Its 5/1 result tests whether substantial late elution begins before 10/1.
Pairing this nicotinate at 1/1 with the selected 5/1 condition and observed 10/1 endpoint brackets its response across eluent strength. The current 1/1 prediction remains untested.
This acyclic aldehyde measured 27.76/69.61 mL at 50/1 (0d588f7534b7a34cb10a). Its 10/1 prediction of 10.16/18.26 mL tests a large condition shift for a scaffold with little supplied coverage.

The bromo acid's recorded 50/1 V2 is −0.10 mL, below V1 of 0.13 mL (129036e0bccc4ff7e848). A 1/1 measurement checks whether this anomalous endpoint is isolated; the record does not support a chemical explanation.

hypotheses.content: Cinnamic acid retains highly condition-sensitive V2: the new 10/1 measurement is 91.31 mL after 46.22 mL at 2/1 and 60.92 mL at 5/1. The earlier simple interpolation hypothesis remains inadequate; loading-solvent volume differs across some records.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How much of the unusual V2 pattern is attributable to eluent ratio versus loading-solvent volume?

hypotheses.content: Eluent-ratio response is strongly molecule-specific. Naphthyl acetate rose from 5.23/13.28 mL at 2/1 to 30.46/50.78 mL at 50/1, while the earlier β-diketone showed much less V1 change. A 20/1 measurement can test the acetate's intermediate response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does naphthyl acetate at 20/1 fall between its measured 2/1 and 50/1 V1/V2 endpoints?

hypotheses.content: Phenylpropanol measured 8.57/16.45 mL at 1/1, 13.06/22.22 mL at 2/1, 34.58/50.00 mL at 5/1, and 51.71/94.93 mL at 10/1. This supports a steep response between 2/1 and 5/1, but V/ul differs across records; transfer to another alcohol is untested.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does naphthylmethanol at 5/1 show comparably late elution?

hypotheses.content: Basic nitrogen compounds show large but inconsistent model errors. Quinoline, dimethylpyridine, and ethyl nicotinate were underpredicted at PE-rich conditions; phenylpyridine at 10/1 was overpredicted, while its 50/1 V2 was underestimated. A single class-wide correction is unsupported.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do nicotinate and phenylpyridine begin their PE-rich V2 increases?

hypotheses.content: Amino substitution does not transfer simply across ester scaffolds: para-amino ethyl benzoate at 5/1 measured 26.80/57.07 mL and was strongly underpredicted, whereas methyl anthranilate at 50/1 measured 6.84/12.43 mL and was strongly overpredicted. Position, ester group, and conditions all differ.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does para-amino ethyl benzoate already elute late at 2/1, and does aminobenzonitrile behave similarly?

hypotheses.content: The enamine ester's measured V2 rises across 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1, reaching 109.68 mL at 20/1. Prior predictions overestimated V2 at 5/1 and 10/1 but underestimated it at 20/1, indicating a slope error rather than a uniform offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: What is the 0/1 endpoint, and how robust is the 20/1 response to the catalogued loading-condition change?

hypotheses.content: The cyclopropyl β-keto ester's V1/V2 rose sharply from 19.45/45.11 mL at 10/1 to 44.45/81.20 mL at 20/1. Prior predictions erred in opposite directions at these ratios, suggesting a missed condition slope; V/ul also differs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 5/1 result locate a gradual rise or a sharp change near 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Nitrobenzophenone at 50/1 has a wide recorded elution interval of about 76.81 mL, unlike a simple late-shift pattern. Its 10/1 response is pending; an intermediate 20/1 measurement can test interval growth.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do nitrobenzophenone V1 and V2 change from pending 10/1 through selected 20/1 to measured 50/1?

hypotheses.content: Conjugated and aromatic carbonyl errors depend on both scaffold and ratio. Dibenzalacetone measured 13.35/35.72 mL at 20/1 and 28.20/68.68 mL at 50/1, while the current model predicts a surprisingly high response at 1/1. Naphthyl acetophenone at 20/1 was predicted accurately, weakening a broad aromatic-ketone error claim.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are dibenzalacetone's measured 1/1 and 10/1 V1/V2 consistent with the model's nonmonotone predictions?

hypotheses.content: The proposed transfer of a large oxygen-rich ester underprediction is weakened: the selected multifunctional ester at 2/1 measured 9.04/18.17 mL, close to its prior prediction, despite the earlier large error for methoxyethyl acetoacetate at 5/1.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural or condition difference explains why the two oxygen-rich esters behaved differently?

hypotheses.content: The bromo acid's recorded 50/1 V2 of −0.10 mL is below its V1 of 0.13 mL, so its elution interval is negative. This is an anomalous recorded endpoint, not evidence for a chemical retention mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does a 1/1 measurement yield a physically ordered V1 and V2 for the same acid?

feedback_interpretation: Round-one measurements narrowed the search to condition-response shapes and transfer boundaries. Phenylpropanol and nicotinate showed large PE-rich shifts; the enamine ester and β-keto ester had ratio-dependent prior errors; para-amino benzoate contradicted a simple amino-ester transfer; and dibenzalacetone plus naphthyl carbonyls showed mixed error directions. I selected intermediate and endpoint conditions for these molecules, plus paired pending experiments, and included one check of the bromo acid's anomalous negative recorded interval.
